subject: Request: carveout & evidence protocol for tenant-managed infra affecting latency
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@helixbio.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helixbio.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Request: carveout & evidence protocol for tenant-managed infra affecting latency

Marcus —

Thanks again for the briefing yesterday. We're excited to move forward with Redwood Private in our VPC, but one item the security and SRE teams flagged before we sign: the SLO/uptime language needs to explicitly account for components we control in our tenant network (hardware WAF appliances, on-prem VPN concentrators, and edge routing devices managed by HelixNet).

Specifically, can Redwood: 
- Add a carveout that excludes HelixBio-controlled network and compute maintenance from any latency/availability non-compliance calculations, provided we follow an evidence protocol?
- Define an evidence exchange process (logs, pcap samples, traceroutes) and an escrow-style clause for disputed incidents where we both retain artifacts for 90 days?

Our ask is not to remove responsibility entirely — we want clear attribution steps so incidents can be triaged without penalizing either side for factors outside their control. Procurement is cc'd because they'll need the final addendum to complete the PO.

Attaching a sketch of our infra boundaries (tenant-infra-diagram.png). Happy to hop on a short call if that helps.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
VP, Infrastructure & Security
HelixBio

Attachments: tenant-infra-diagram.png
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@helixbio.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout & evidence protocol for tenant-managed infra affecting latency

Samira —

Appreciate the clear ask and the diagram. We're aligned on the goal: reasonable attribution so neither party is penalized for the other's control plane. High-level proposal from our side: 

1) Define "Customer-Controlled Components" (CCC) as the tenant-owned hardware and tenant-managed network functions listed in your diagram. 
2) Exclude performance events from Redwood uptime/latency SLOs when (a) the CCC manifests clear errors or maintenance, AND (b) HelixBio supplies the evidence artifacts described below within a 7-day window. 
3) Evidence protocol: traceroutes, sampled pcap (redacted), controller logs, and time-synced system metrics. We propose a mutually-agreed retention window of 90 days. 
4) Escrow / dispute path: if parties disagree on attribution, preserve artifacts in an encrypted archive (Redwood-hosted, customer-accessible) for 90 days while we run a joint investigation.

I've drafted a short addendum that implements this flow and includes an example of how p95 latency reporting will be computed with and without CCC events. Draft attached: Helix_SLA_Addendum_Draft_v1.pdf

Neha — can you review for legal language and confirm if the escrow/archive framing needs specific verbatim? Evelyn — please flag any operational concerns (retention, evidence formats, signing access).

Samira — if this looks directionally right we'll circulate redlines and aim to incorporate into the master services agreement (MSA).

Best,
Marcus
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Helix_SLA_Addendum_Draft_v1.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@helixbio.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Request: carveout & evidence protocol for tenant-managed infra affecting latency

Samira —

Forwarding with redlines. We added: 
- A clause that requires "good faith and timeliness" for evidence submission (within 7 days), failing which standard SLO calculations apply. 
- Minimum artifact formatting (timestamped traceroutes with hop latency, csv of sampled p95/p99 metrics, and a hash manifest for pcaps). 
- Language clarifying Redwood retains the right to independently verify artifacts and to aggregate metrics for trend analysis. 
- A limited indemnity carveout for incidents where CCC is proven to be the primary cause (subject to a mutual investigation and documented evidence).

Please review the attached redlined PDF. If HelixBio is comfortable with these terms we can prepare a DocuSign packet and loop in Procurement.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if you want to walk through any line items.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Neha / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and thoughtful redlines. The evidence formats and the 7-day submission window are acceptable to HelixBio. A couple of small asks from procurement: 
- Can the DocuSign packet include a single signature block for both the SLA addendum and the related PO reference (HLX-PO-7789)?
- Can Redwood confirm the encrypted archive will be accessible to HelixBio for the 90-day retention period (we need read access for investigations)?

If you can confirm those two items, we can route the packet for signature on our side and target execution before EOW. Appreciate the pragmatic approach here.

Best regards,
Samira
